intro.title: Race Condition Fix
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple React app that fetches and displays user data from a mock API. You will learn how to identify and fix a race condition, a common bug where the order of asynchronous operations affects the final result. The core concept involves using JavaScript's AbortController to cancel outdated fetch requests, ensuring only the latest data is shown. You will work with React hooks like useState and useEffect, TypeScript for type safety, and the Fetch API for making HTTP calls.
intro.usecase: Race conditions frequently occur in modern web applications when multiple asynchronous operations compete for the same resources. In product dashboards, users might rapidly toggle filters or date ranges, causing overlapping API calls that can display stale or incorrect data. E-commerce sites face this when users quickly add/remove items from their cart while inventory updates are still processing. Search interfaces with auto-complete can show results from outdated queries if newer requests complete faster than earlier ones. Understanding and fixing race conditions is essential for building reliable, predictable user experiences.
